Strait of Hormuz Status: October 11, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  225 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
11 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.72 + 0.42 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 gCaptain reports more tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz and a US strike hit a cargo ship, with the attacker of the tankers not identified by any maritime authority.

02 Iran has rejected the US reply to its seven conditions for reopening the strait as insufficient, per India Today, leaving the channel between Iran and the United States deadlocked.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz saw further vessel strikes on October 11, with gCaptain reporting additional tankers hit and a US strike on a cargo ship; who fired on the tankers has not been identified by any maritime authority in this feed. Iranian state media claim, separately, that a supertanker exploded and caught fire after striking a mine in the southern part of the strait, a claim originating with Mehr News and relayed by gCaptain, Around Prague, WANA News Agency, and Shafaq News; it is an Iranian state media claim and no maritime authority in this feed has addressed it. Breakingthenews.net reports a tanker was hit by a projectile in the strait, and New York Post reports that Iran set a supertanker ablaze after a vessel was struck while said to be breaking the blockade, with the attacker not identified by any independent maritime authority cited in this feed. The Jerusalem Post reports Iran's rejection of the US reply to its conditions for reopening the strait as insufficient. The Indian Express reports India has condemned attacks in the strait, with two Indian seafarers missing. Brent settled at $104.72 at Friday's close, up 0.42% on the last session before the close; futures are shut. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Between August 1 and September 26, Hellenic Shipping News reports, 10 sanctioned vessels switched to Nicaraguan MMSI numbers, 8 of them first heard on the new number near the strait. As of 21:20 UTC, 152 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.

Cite as
Straits, “Hormuz daily brief”, 11 Oct 2026 .
